Assimilating new chickens into your flock / How to introduce assimilate Pullets with your old birds

I didn't watch the video since I am currently at work but this is the process that I followed in the past.

I have a small run that shares a fence with the large run. Once the pullets are out of the brooder I move them to the small pen. It is just 2x4 welded wire so the older chickens always stick their heads through to peck the smaller chickens, so the pullets get used to bullying pretty quickly and know who to steer clear of. Once the young hens start laying I start to integrate by letting both groups out in the yard at the same time a couple times. Eventually the bolder of the young hens follow the older hens into the large coop once they put themselves up for the night. Once that happens I wait until dark then grab whatever young ones didn't go to the large coop and place them on the top rung of roost with the older chickens.

Once in the big run some of the pullets will want to sleep on the ground next to the fence that the big run shares with their old pen for nostalgia reasons, but I just go out each night and put them on the roost and sooner or later they catch on.
Thanks for the tips. Sounds like you've got a good system going. The young ones didn't get bullied when they were placed on the top rung with the older chickens?

Chickens can't see in a dark at all, once it gets dark they basically just shut down. So you can take the young chickens and shove them right beside the bullies on the top and they just sleep together. Then in the morning they wake up side by side and it helps the older ones accept the newer ones. It isn't instant, but over time it works out.
